close_reason:
Superseded by bd:JMAP-1j9k.9 (closed by commit b6d2ebb on 2026-05-17), via the cascade through this bead's blocker JMAP-tjvm.16 (closed 2026-05-17 with identical reasoning). The workspace adopted the OPPOSITE policy: public method-input Params structs in *-client crates do NOT use #[non_exhaustive]; forward-compat for future spec-defined fields is the flatten-ed 'extra: serde_json::Map<String, serde_json::Value>' field per workspace AGENTS.md extras-preservation policy.

Adding #[non_exhaustive] to MetadataChangesParams would now be the regression — the struct already follows the workspace-canonical shape: filter_related_type + filter_metadata_type typed fields + 'extra' flatten field with #[serde(flatten, default, skip_serializing_if = ...)]. Verified at crate-jmap-metadata-client/src/methods/mod.rs:85-125. The vendor-extras path is tested at lines 562-570 (metadata_changes_params_propagates_vendor_extras).

The Mark-authored 2026-05-15 comment explicitly correctly identified the canonical-template propagation rule and parked the work behind canonical mail-client; that canonical closed with the policy reversal, and the propagation now correctly resolves to no-op-and-close rather than land-and-propagate. The bead's premise (struct-literal construction break on future typed-field addition) is real but the workspace policy decision was to accept that break by design — the extras flatten field provides forward-compat for vendor/site fields, and typed-field addition is left as an intentional breaking change tied to a minor version bump.

Sibling wzq9.29 (the other 4 metadata-client params structs) closed under the same reasoning earlier in this do-beads session.
description:
src/methods/mod.rs:40-61 — MetadataChangesParams is declared as:

    #[derive(Debug, Default, serde::Serialize)]
    #[serde(rename_all = \"camelCase\")]
    pub struct MetadataChangesParams { … }

Missing #[non_exhaustive]. The struct has public fields filter_related_type, filter_metadata_type, extra. Once 0.1.0 ships, callers can construct it with struct-literal syntax positionally:

    MetadataChangesParams { filter_related_type: None, filter_metadata_type: None, extra: Map::new() }

Adding a typed field later (say a future draft revision adds 'sinceState' filter at the params level, or 'forAccount' or any new typed knob) requires every caller to update their struct-literal — a breaking change for downstream callers.

#[non_exhaustive] forces callers to use Default::default() + field-update syntax, which keeps additions non-breaking. The workspace policy at AGENTS.md 'Extras-preservation policy' lists struct shapes that should be #[non_exhaustive]; this is one. (Note: mail-client EmailGetParams, EmailCopyParams, MailboxSetParams etc. are ALSO missing #[non_exhaustive] — this is workspace-wide divergence from the canonical extras-preservation requirement. Fix needs to propagate; canonical mail-client should land it first.)

Trigger: downstream caller using struct-literal syntax breaks when a new typed field lands. Fix: add #[non_exhaustive] to the struct.
title: MetadataChangesParams not #[non_exhaustive] — adding a typed field is breaking
